steps.prompt: $\lfloor 3.7 \rfloor = 3$, but $\lfloor -3.7 \rfloor = -4$. Why do you think the second one isn't $-3$?

cards.title: Floor and ceiling
cards.body: $\lfloor x \rfloor$ (floor) is the greatest integer $\leq x$: round DOWN. $\lceil x \rceil$ (ceiling) is the smallest integer $\geq x$: round UP. Down means towards $-\infty$, so $\lfloor -2.5 \rfloor = -3$. $\lfloor x \rfloor = n$ means $n \leq x < n + 1$.

cards.title: Worked example: counting multiples
cards.problem: How many multiples of $7$ are there from $50$ to $200$?

steps.text: From $1$ to $200$ there are $\lfloor \frac{200}{7} \rfloor = 28$ multiples of $7$.
From $1$ to $49$ there are $\lfloor \frac{49}{7} \rfloor = 7$. Take them away: $28 - 7 = 21$.

cards.title: Piecewise functions
cards.body: A piecewise function uses different rules on different parts of the number line. First decide WHICH part the input is in, including the boundary (is it $<$ or $\geq$?), then use that rule.

cards.title: Worked example: two rules
cards.problem: Let $f(x) = 2x + 1$ when $x < 3$ and $f(x) = x^2 - 4$ when $x \geq 3$. Find $f(f(1))$.

cards.title: The common trap: negatives and boundaries
cards.body: The floor of a negative number goes MORE negative: $\lfloor -3.2 \rfloor = -4$. A boundary value belongs to exactly one piece; read $<$ and $\geq$ carefully. And $\lfloor x \rfloor + \lfloor y \rfloor$ is not always $\lfloor x + y \rfloor$.

prompts: How do you count the multiples of $k$ between two numbers? Write the steps.
